faqs.question: Is All Hallows' Eve the same day as Halloween?
faqs.answer: Yes. Halloween is 31 October, and the word itself is a Scots shortening of Allhalloweven, the evening before All Hallows (All Saints' Day) on 1 November. People who say 'Halloween Eve' usually mean 30 October, the night before.

faqs.question: What can I text someone on the night before Halloween?
faqs.answer: Send a short countdown line on the evening of 30 October, such as 'One more sleep until Halloween. Lay out the costume, hide the good chocolate.' Keep it playful and add their name. 30 October is a Friday in 2026 and a Saturday in 2027.

faqs.question: Is it all right for a Christian to send Happy Halloween wishes?
faqs.answer: Many Christians keep 31 October as the vigil of All Saints and are glad to receive either greeting, while some prefer to avoid Halloween altogether. If you are unsure, send an All Hallows' Eve or All Saints' Day greeting, which names the feast rather than the costumes.

faqs.question: What is the difference between All Saints' Day and All Souls' Day?
faqs.answer: All Saints' Day on 1 November is a joyful feast honouring the saints, including those with no feast day of their own. All Souls' Day on 2 November is for praying for and remembering the dead; Uhrin's 2026 study dates it as a Catholic day of remembrance to the 10th century.

faqs.question: Is Día de los Muertos the same as Halloween?
faqs.answer: No. It is a Mexican indigenous festivity, inscribed on UNESCO's intangible heritage list in 2008, in which families lay petals, candles and offerings to welcome dead relatives home for a short visit. Send Día de los Muertos lines only to people who celebrate it, and never with a costume joke.

faqs.question: What should I write to someone grieving on All Souls' Day?
faqs.answer: Name the person who died, keep it to one or two lines and make clear no reply is needed, for example 'Today I'm remembering [name] with you. No reply needed.' A call or a visit to the grave together often says more than any message.

faqs.question: Why is it sometimes spelled Hallowe'en?
faqs.answer: Hallowe'en is an older alternative spelling listed by Wiktionary. The apostrophe marks the letters squeezed out of 'even', the archaic form of eve, so Hallowe'en literally reads as hallow-even.

faqs.question: Can I send a Halloween greeting early so it opens on 31 October?
faqs.answer: Yes. SubhSandesh's premium Halloween page has an optional unlock time: share the link on 30 October and, until the time you set, it shows only their name and a countdown. A plain text can simply be scheduled in most messaging apps.

faqs.question: What does Allhallowtide mean?
faqs.answer: Allhallowtide means the time at or near All Hallows, usually counted as three days: 31 October, 1 November and 2 November. In Slovakia the same three days are called Dušičky, 'little souls'.

faqs.question: Can I send All Hallows' Eve greetings to a church WhatsApp group?
faqs.answer: Yes; reverent lines such as 'A blessed All Hallows' Eve. May the saints we honour tomorrow pray for us tonight.' suit a parish group, and you can add the service time. SubhSandesh's Halloween pages greet one person, so they are not the tool for a group message.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Eve Greetings for 30 October and All Hallows' Eve

Halloween eve greetings belong to two different nights. Most people mean 30 October, the night before Halloween; churches mean 31 October itself, since the word Halloween shortens All Hallows' Eve, the vigil before the 1 November feast of All Saints. Below are 52 original greetings, including gentle lines for 1 and 2 November.

Leaving it late is normal: in SubhSandesh's nearest festival analogue, Raksha Bandhan 2026, 27.0% of 89 pages were made the day before and 49.4% on the day itself. Across the platform, 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone, so every line here fits one screen; neither figure is Halloween data.

## Which night is Halloween Eve, 30 or 31 October?

Halloween is already an eve. The [Wiktionary etymology of Halloween](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Halloween) traces the word to a Scots shortening of Allhalloweven: Allhallowmas, the old name for All Saints' Day, plus even, an archaic form of eve.

So "Halloween Eve" is literally the eve of an eve. In everyday speech it means 30 October (a Friday in 2026, a Saturday in 2027); just make the date clear.

## Allhallowtide: what 31 October, 1 November and 2 November each mark

[Allhallowtide](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/Allhallowtide) means the time at or near All Hallows. Michal Uhrin's 2026 study in the open-access journal [Český lid](https://ceskylid.avcr.cz/cz/article/itm-3033938), based on 2023 and 2024 fieldwork in a Slovak village, describes it as a triduum: All Saints' Eve on 31 October, All Saints' Day on 1 November and All Souls' Day on 2 November.

Uhrin notes that 1 November first honoured saints with no feast day of their own, and that 2 November has been a Catholic day for the dead since the 10th century. Villagers there tidy graves and light candles on them; until about the 1970s, people prayed until plain 10 cm wax candles burned down.

## 52 Halloween eve greetings, from 30 October to 2 November

The six groups run in date order, playful to quiet. Swap the brackets for real names.

### 1. Night-before-Halloween countdown texts (30 October)

Send these on the evening of 30 October to anyone who loves the build-up. Playful, never gory.

- "One more sleep until Halloween. Lay out the costume, hide the good chocolate."
- "T-minus 24 hours. Is your pumpkin carved, or still just a vegetable?"
- "Tomorrow the doorbell gets busy. Tonight, we rest and stockpile."
- "Halloween Eve check-in: costume, sweets bowl, courage. What's missing?"
- "The ghosts are rehearsing. Showtime is tomorrow at dusk."
- "Last calm night before the sugar rush. Sleep well, [name]."
- "Tomorrow I'll be a witch. Tonight I'm just someone who misses you."
- "Countdown update: one night left and the cat already looks suspicious."
- "Pumpkin carved, candle bought, lighter missing. A normal Halloween Eve, then."
- "Fair warning: tomorrow's costume involves a bedsheet and zero shame."
- "Wishing you a quiet Halloween Eve and a loud, sticky Halloween tomorrow."
- "Tomorrow you get to be a dragon, [child's name]. Tonight, be a sleepy one."

### 2. Traditional All Hallows' Eve greetings (31 October)

For parish newsletters, church chats and believers keeping 31 October as a vigil. Reverent and hopeful.

- "A blessed All Hallows' Eve. May the saints we honour tomorrow pray for us tonight."
- "On this vigil of All Saints, thanks for every faithful life that lit the way."
- "Wishing our parish family a peaceful All Hallows' Eve and a joyful feast tomorrow."
- "Tonight we keep vigil; tomorrow we celebrate the great cloud of witnesses."
- "May the saints shine brighter than any lantern tonight."
- "Grace and peace to you on All Hallows' Eve, from all of us at [church name]."
- "Blessings on this holy eve. May the saints' courage find a home in us."
- "A prayerful All Hallows' Eve to you and yours. Evening prayer begins at [time]."
- "On the eve of All Saints, may every candle in our windows be a small prayer."
- "Peace to you this All Hallows' Eve, and to everyone you carry in your heart."

### 3. Blended greetings: costumes tonight, saints tomorrow (31 October)

For families who trick-or-treat and attend a service on 1 November. A wink at the costumes, a nod to the feast.

- "Happy Halloween and a blessed All Saints' Day. Sweets tonight, service at ten."
- "Tonight we dress as monsters; tomorrow we remember the saints. Enjoy both."
- "Wishing you a happy All Hallows' Eve, the original name for tonight's fun."
- "The costumes are borrowed, the candles are real. Happy Halloween and a holy feast."
- "Trick-or-treat first, then early to bed: the All Saints' service won't wait."
- "Pumpkin lanterns tonight, church candles tomorrow: may both glow."
- "Happy Hallowe'en. Our little ghost wants a saint story at bedtime tomorrow."
- "Enjoy the spooky bits tonight. Tomorrow the eve becomes a feast."

### 4. All Saints' Day messages (1 November)

All Saints' Day is a feast, so these are joyful. Send them to godparents or anyone whose goodness you admire.

- "Happy All Saints' Day. Thank you for showing me what a good life looks like."
- "On All Saints' Day I thought of you, my unofficial saint of patience."
- "Blessings on All Saints' Day. May we keep their company one day."
- "Happy All Saints' Day, godmother. Your prayers carried me further than you know."
- "Today the Church honours every saint, named and unnamed. You are my favourite unnamed one."
- "Joyful feast of All Saints to our whole [choir]. Thanks for every hymn."
- "Happy feast day to a friend who shares a saint's name and lives up to it."

### 5. All Souls' Day remembrance messages (2 November)

All Souls' Day is for remembering the dead, so keep these short and name the person. In a [2020 Nursing Open study of 61 bereaved parents](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC7729787) from 14 countries or cultural groups, Cuban families reported lighting candles for the dead on birthdays and first anniversaries.

- "On All Souls' Day, [name] is in my thoughts. A candle is burning for them here."
- "Today I'm remembering [name] with you. No reply needed."
- "On All Souls' Day, praying that [name] rests in peace and that you feel held."
- "Eternal rest grant unto [name], O Lord. Holding your family in prayer today."
- "Your first All Souls' Day without [name]. I'm here, today and after."
- "I visited [name]'s grave and left flowers from both of us."
- "Still telling [name]'s terrible jokes. Remembering them with love this All Souls' Day."
- "No words fix this, so just these: [name] is remembered, and so are you."
- "May everyone we have lost be at peace, and may we be gentle with ourselves."

### 6. Día de los Muertos lines, sent with respect (1–2 November)

The Day of the Dead is its own festival, not a Mexican Halloween. UNESCO's heritage listing for the [indigenous festivity dedicated to the dead](https://ich.unesco.org/en/RL/indigenous-festivity-dedicated-to-the-dead-00054) (inscribed 2008) describes families laying petals, candles and offerings to welcome dead relatives home for a short visit.

Mexican parents in the Nursing Open study described altars where the spirit is believed to visit, with toys and candy for children. Send these only to people who celebrate.

- "Thinking of you as you build the ofrenda. Which of [name]'s dishes goes on it?"
- "Wishing you a beautiful Día de los Muertos, full of marigolds and stories about [name]."
- "May every candle on your altar light the way home for the ones you love."
- "Saving a place in my heart for [name] this Día de los Muertos."
- "Hope the pan de muerto is still warm when the family shares it."
- "Que en paz descansen, and may their stories keep growing." (May they rest in peace.)

## Halloween eve greetings by date: tone and example for 4 days

Each date with its occasion, tone and one example from the lists. Weekdays are for 2026 and 2027.

| Date | Occasion | Tone | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 October (Fri 2026, Sat 2027) | Night before Halloween | Playful countdown | "One more sleep until Halloween." |
| 31 October (Sat 2026, Sun 2027) | Halloween, or All Hallows' Eve | Playful, or reverent for church | "A blessed All Hallows' Eve." |
| 1 November (Sun 2026, Mon 2027) | All Saints' Day | Joyful, grateful | "Blessings on All Saints' Day." |
| 2 November (Mon 2026, Tue 2027) | All Souls' Day; Día de los Muertos runs 1–2 November | Gentle remembrance | "Today I'm remembering [name] with you." |

Humour belongs to 30 and 31 October and drains out by 2 November. Mixing them up is what a recipient remembers.

## When to send each greeting, and how late is too late

Send countdown texts on the evening of 30 October, church greetings early on 31 October, and the rest on their own days. Last-minute is normal: in Raksha Bandhan 2026, 86.1% of the 79 on-time pages were made within a day of the festival (not Halloween data).

Grief is private, so it helps that 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators already add a password before sharing. Write All Souls' notes the night before if that is when the words come.

## Turning a 30 October greeting into a Halloween card

When a text feels too small, our [interactive Halloween card with photos and music](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) is a five-minute build: both names, a letter, as many as six photos and one word for the pumpkin. They knock on a small haunted house, carve the lantern until your word lights up and read your letter by torchlight.

Partner, bestie, family and kids modes change the closing question, and you hear by email when they first reply. For a night-before send, the [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) has an optional unlock time: share it on 30 October and it shows only their name and a countdown until then.

## When a playful Halloween card is the wrong choice

Both pages are playful by design and end in a boo question and a Boo License. They suit groups 1 and 3, not the reverent lines in groups 2, 4, 5 and 6.

For someone grieving on 2 November, a plain text, a letter or a call is kinder. One of Uhrin's interviewees says you must visit the grave and light a candle even after a night shift; if you live nearby, go with them. Neither page is a parish newsletter, and both are in English only.

## Sources

- Wiktionary: Halloween; Allhallowtide (undated).
- Uhrin, *Český lid*, 25 March 2026.
- Hidalgo et al., *Nursing Open*, 2 October 2020.
- UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, inscribed 2008.
